title: Lesson 01 – Accounting Information Systems: An Overview
description: Examines systems concepts, data versus information, AIS components, business processes, and how AIS supports strategy and value creation.
subject: ACC2475 - Accounting Information Systems and ERP Applications

questions.question: A production department chooses to exceed its budget so the organization can deliver products on time. This situation best illustrates which systems principle?
options: Goal congruence between subsystems and the organization
questions.answer: Goal congruence between subsystems and the organization
questions.rationale: Subsystems should support the overall organizational goal even if it harms their own objectives.

questions.question: Which situation best demonstrates the transformation of data into information?
options: Recording the numbers 3, 99, and 20000 in a database
Listing a date, customer name, and item number without explanation
Organizing transaction facts into a structured sales invoice
Storing raw transaction logs without processing them
questions.answer: Organizing transaction facts into a structured sales invoice
questions.rationale: Information is created when raw facts are organized and processed to give meaning.

questions.question: Which characteristic of useful information ensures different decision makers derive the same conclusion from identical data?
questions.rationale: Consistency ensures information is presented uniformly across reports and time periods.

questions.question: A firm introduces automated inventory tracking to reduce duplicate data entry across departments. Which systems concept is being applied?
questions.rationale: Integration reduces duplication of recording, storing, and reporting information.

questions.question: When an organization gathers excessive reports that managers cannot effectively interpret, which problem is most likely occurring?
questions.rationale: Too much information reduces decision quality and increases costs.

questions.question: Which type of information is typically required by government regulators and external authorities?
questions.rationale: Mandatory information must be provided to comply with regulatory requirements.

questions.question: In AIS design, why must organizations evaluate both costs and benefits of information?
options: Information must be produced regardless of cost
Information is valuable only when benefits exceed production costs
Costs cannot be estimated during system design
questions.answer: Information is valuable only when benefits exceed production costs
questions.rationale: Information has value when the benefit of decisions made from it exceeds its cost.

questions.question: Which AIS function directly supports managerial planning and control activities?
options: Transforming data into decision useful information
Restricting information access to external parties
questions.answer: Transforming data into decision useful information
questions.rationale: AIS converts transaction data into meaningful information for management decisions.

questions.question: A company records sales transactions, stores them in databases, and later produces revenue analysis reports. Which AIS function is illustrated?
questions.rationale: AIS converts stored transaction data into reports and decision relevant information.

questions.question: Which component of an AIS ensures that organizational data remains protected from unauthorized access?
questions.rationale: Controls safeguard assets and protect the integrity of information.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains machine readable data?
options: Data stored only in printed reports
Data formatted so computers can process it automatically
questions.answer: Data formatted so computers can process it automatically
questions.rationale: Machine readable formats allow computer systems to process data efficiently.

questions.question: Which business process represents the exchange of goods or services for payment from customers?
questions.rationale: The revenue cycle involves sales and collection activities.

questions.question: A company implementing blockchain removes the need for centralized record keeping. Which characteristic of blockchain enables this?
questions.rationale: Blockchain stores records across a decentralized network rather than a single location.

questions.question: Which emerging technology allows multiple operating systems to run simultaneously on one physical machine?
questions.rationale: Virtualization enables multiple systems to run on a single physical computer.

questions.question: Which factor most directly influences how an AIS should be structured to support competitive advantage?
questions.rationale: AIS design must align with organizational strategy.

questions.question: The concept of a value chain emphasizes that organizational value is created primarily through:
options: Sequential activities that enhance product value
Increasing the number of internal departments
questions.answer: Sequential activities that enhance product value
questions.rationale: Value increases as products move through linked activities in the value chain.

questions.question: Which AIS benefit most directly improves coordination with suppliers and distributors?
questions.rationale: AIS enhances communication and coordination across the supply chain.

questions.question: Which scenario most clearly demonstrates discretionary information usage?
options: Submitting financial reports required by regulators
Producing compliance documentation for government agencies
questions.rationale: Internal users primarily use discretionary information for decision making.

questions.question: In blockchain systems, cryptographic hashing primarily ensures:
questions.rationale: Hashes link blocks and prevent unauthorized modification.

questions.question: Which AIS component includes the computers, communication networks, and hardware devices used to run the system?
questions.rationale: IT infrastructure provides the technological foundation for AIS operations.

questions.question: Which situation best represents goal conflict within an organization?
options: A department achieving its targets while supporting overall organizational objectives
Two departments pursuing objectives that undermine each other
All departments aligning their strategies with corporate goals
questions.answer: Two departments pursuing objectives that undermine each other
questions.rationale: Goal conflict occurs when subsystem goals contradict each other or the organization.

questions.question: The [dropdown_1] cycle manages acquiring goods and services from suppliers, while the [dropdown_2] cycle focuses on selling goods and collecting payment.
questions.rationale: Expenditure cycles handle purchases while revenue cycles handle sales.

questions.question: AIS collects and stores [dropdown_1] about events and resources and later converts them into [dropdown_2] useful for decision making.
questions.rationale: AIS converts raw data into meaningful information.

questions.question: In blockchain processing, transactions are first [dropdown_1] before being grouped into a [dropdown_2].
questions.rationale: Transactions are validated and then grouped into blocks in blockchain systems.

questions.question: A ________ is a set of interrelated components that interact to achieve a goal.
questions.rationale: A system consists of interacting components working toward a common objective.

questions.question: When subsystem objectives align with organizational objectives, the condition is called ________.
questions.rationale: Goal congruence occurs when subsystem goals support overall organizational goals.

questions.question: Embedding sensors into devices so they connect and communicate through the internet describes the ________ concept.
questions.rationale: IoT refers to internet connected physical devices that share data.

questions.question: Which activities represent major AIS business functions?
options: Transforming data into decision relevant information
answer: Transforming data into decision relevant information
questions.rationale: AIS collects data, converts it to information, and safeguards assets.

questions.question: Which elements are core components of an Accounting Information System?
questions.rationale: AIS components include people, procedures, data, software, IT infrastructure, and controls.

questions.question: Which benefits may result from a well designed AIS?
questions.rationale: AIS improves decision quality, efficiency, and control mechanisms.

questions.question: Match each concept with its description.

matchPairs.right: Raw facts stored in a system

questions.rationale: These definitions distinguish raw facts from processed and usable data.

questions.question: Match each business cycle with its primary focus.
questions.rationale: Transaction cycles categorize recurring business processes.

questions.question: Match each emerging technology with its description.

matchPairs.right: Running multiple systems on one physical machine
Accessing computing resources remotely via internet
Devices embedded with sensors connected to networks

questions.rationale: These technologies represent key innovations influencing AIS development.

questions.question: Explain how an Accounting Information System supports organizational decision making and operational control across different departments.
questions.rationale: The answer should explain how AIS gathers data, converts it to information, and supports management control.

questions.question: Discuss how an Accounting Information System contributes to value creation within the organizational value chain and supply chain.
questions.rationale: AIS enhances coordination, improves efficiency, and supports value creation across business activities.
